memos.headline: S04 and S10 Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; S02 in Freefall, S08 and S05 Lagging
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market across this universe. S04 and S10 are the standout leaders: S04 sits just 0.6% off its 52-week high with 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +17.5%, while S10 is only 3.7% off its high with +15.9% relative strength over the same period—both well above their 50-day and 200-day means. S06 is similarly strong, trading near highs with RSI 68.2 and +6.2% 12-week relative strength, though I'd want to see a pullback toward the 50-day before adding. On the other side, S02 is a disaster: down 51.7% from its 52-week high, 40% below its 200-day mean, RSI 36.6, and -44.4% relative strength over 12 weeks—this is a broken chart with no sign of a base. S08 and S05 are also below their 200-day means with negative relative strength, and S01 is weakening with RSI under 40 and negative 4-week momentum. I would flip my S04 view to neutral if it breaks below 435 (roughly its 50-day mean), and I'd reconsider S02 only on a sustained close above 370.

views.note: Trading within 0.6% of 52-week high, RSI 69, +17.5% 12w relative strength vs SPY—textbook leadership; would reassess below ~435.
Up +19.2% over 12 weeks, 14.6% above 50-day mean, strong +15.9% relative strength; higher ATR warrants tighter sizing but trend is clearly up.
Near 52-week high with +13.2% 26-week return and +6.2% 12w relative strength; RSI 68.2 is elevated but not overbought, low ATR of 1.57% is attractive.
Strong 4-week surge of +10.7% and best 4w relative strength at +8.7%, but RSI 71.4 is overbought and 12w relative strength is still -4.9%—wait for a pullback to confirm.

RSI 39.8, below both 50-day and 200-day means, -5.8% 4w relative strength—weakening momentum with no catalyst visible in price.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Lead on Margin Expansion; S07 and S09 Show Earnings Compression
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable, high-margin growers and names where earnings power is deteriorating. S10 stands out with 69.2% YoY revenue growth, a 42.6% net margin, and only $8.46B in total debt — the cleanest balance sheet in the group. S05 delivered $34.54B in net income on a 38.3% net margin with net income up 46.0% YoY, while S04 posted a 36.9% margin and 17.7% net income growth on modest leverage of $42.88B. On the other end, S07 is contracting badly with revenue down 9.8% and net income down 29.8% YoY on $31.74B of debt — a leverage-to-earnings profile I want no part of — and S09 is essentially flat on revenue with a 6.2% decline in net income and a thin 9.3% margin. I would need to see margin stabilization or a meaningful debt reduction in S07 and S09 before reconsidering.

views.note: 69.2% revenue growth, 42.6% net margin, and minimal debt of $8.46B make this the strongest fundamental profile in the universe.
38.3% net margin with 46% YoY net income growth and low debt of $14.79B signals durable, expanding earnings power.
36.9% net margin, 13.3% revenue growth, and 17.7% net income growth on manageable $42.88B debt is a solid compounder.
Revenue up 8.6% and net income up 64.2% are encouraging, but the 11.0% net margin and $58.75B debt leave less room for error; I need to see margin durability.
26.0% net margin is respectable but revenue growth of only 5.1% and $92.20B in total debt suggest limited upside from here without re-acceleration.
32.3% margin is attractive but $407.22B in total debt dwarfs the group; earnings growth of 9.1% needs to accelerate to justify that leverage.
Flat revenue (+0.1%), declining net income (-6.2%), and a thin 9.3% margin on $32.82B debt signal cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.
Revenue down 9.8% and net income down 29.8% with $31.74B in debt is a deteriorating earnings profile; would reconsider only if margins stabilize above 18%.
Revenue grew 9.8% but a 5.7% net margin on $81.27B debt is the thinnest margin-to-leverage ratio in the group; net income trend unavailable.
19.1% margin is decent but revenue declined 2.1% and net income was flat (+0.4%); need top-line re-acceleration to get constructive.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Cooling Labor Market and Benign CPI — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Neutral Banks
memos.body: I see the macro regime as a prolonged pause with an easing bias: the Fed has held the upper bound at 4.50% for three consecutive months while the unemployment rate has drifted up 40bp year-over-year to 4.30% and CPI inflation has moderated to just 2.4% y/y. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+91bp over 12 months to +0.44pp), consistent with the market pricing eventual cuts, though the 10y yield at 4.38% has actually edged higher over three months (+14bp), suggesting term premium is building. I have moderate conviction that the next move is a cut — a further rise in unemployment above 4.5% or a CPI print below 2.3% y/y would solidify that call and push me to higher conviction on duration-sensitive names. A re-acceleration in CPI above 3% would flip the regime back to hawkish hold and I would rotate defensively into staples and energy.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from easing bias with CPI at 2.4% and rising unemployment signaling eventual cuts.
Growth/tech sector should outperform as real rates are poised to decline with inflation moderating and the Fed on pause.
Banks benefit from a steeper curve (+91bp y/y in 10y-2y spread) but rising unemployment threatens credit quality; net neutral.
Staples offer defensive value if the slowdown deepens but lack upside in a soft-landing scenario; hold neutral for now.
Cyclicals face headwinds from a softening labor market and still-restrictive policy rates at 4.50%.
Energy lacks a clear macro catalyst; moderate inflation and slowing growth create an ambiguous demand outlook.

memos.headline: Earnings-Driven Sentiment Divergence: S04 and S10 Stand Out Positively While S08 Flags Negative and S02 Shows Leadership Churn
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions and filing cadence across the universe as the primary sentiment signals available. S04's +7.6% reaction to its April 30 results filing is the strongest positive tone shift in the group, and S10's +3.2% pop on May 28 earnings confirms a constructive narrative—both suggest the market was positively surprised and sentiment may still have room to run. On the negative side, S08's -3.7% drop on its May 1 earnings release, followed by an 'Other Events' filing on May 12, signals deteriorating sentiment that may not yet be fully washed out. S02 has filed four 8-Ks since late April, three involving director/officer departures or appointments, which is an unusually high cadence of leadership turnover that I read as a potential narrative risk even if the market hasn't reacted visibly yet. For S01, the June 9 officer departure/appointment ('Arnold Announcement') combined with a Deutsche Bank presentation days earlier suggests a management narrative in flux—I'd stay neutral until the dust settles.

views.note: Strongest positive earnings reaction in the universe at +7.6%; sentiment momentum likely not fully priced given the magnitude of the surprise.
Solid +3.2% earnings reaction on May 28 suggests positive sentiment shift with the print still relatively fresh.
Negative -3.7% earnings reaction followed by an Other Events filing suggests deteriorating narrative that may have further to run.
Four filings in six weeks with three involving officer departures/appointments signals unusual leadership churn—a latent negative sentiment catalyst.
Management change plus investor presentation in quick succession creates narrative uncertainty; waiting for clarity.
Muted +0.6% earnings reaction and routine subsequent filings suggest no strong sentiment catalyst in either direction.
Flat +0.4% earnings reaction and only a routine shareholder vote filing since—no discernible sentiment trend.
Essentially flat -0.1% earnings reaction; no narrative shift evident from filings.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Falling Fast but VIX Spike and Oil Surge Signal Residual Geopolitical Risk
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 44% over three months to 315.71, suggesting the worst of the tariff/sanctions shock narrative is fading, yet VIX has jumped 22% in the past month to 22.17 and WTI crude surged nearly 19% to $75.89/bbl—a combination that points to an energy-security or supply-disruption catalyst still in play. HY spreads at 3.16% remain benign, down 3bp over three months, so credit markets are not pricing a structural policy break. The 10y-2y spread widening of +19bp over three months to 0.44pp is consistent with a reflationary impulse, possibly tied to fiscal or trade-policy shifts. Without granular GDELT event data on specific sanctions or export-control actions, I have limited conviction on individual names; the 8-K filings across the universe are generic Reg FD or Other Events disclosures that do not reveal direct geopolitical exposure. My base case is that the macro policy backdrop is improving but the oil/VIX divergence warrants caution on energy-sensitive or supply-chain-concentrated names until the source of the crude move clarifies.

views.note: Only a single generic 8.01 8-K; no identifiable geopolitical exposure from available evidence, so I stay flat.
Three 8-K filings in quick succession suggest active corporate communication but without content detail I cannot assess geopolitical risk direction.
Two early-May 8-Ks (Other Events) coincide with the period of peak policy uncertainty; declining EPU since then is mildly supportive but insufficient for a directional call.
Active Reg FD disclosures in June alongside a VIX spike suggest the company is managing market-sensitive information; I lack detail to take a side.
With WTI up 19% in a month and VIX elevated, any name with energy-cost or supply-chain concentration risk faces headwinds; single Reg FD filing offers no offset.
One Reg FD filing and benign HY spreads suggest no acute stress, but the oil-VIX divergence keeps me from going long without more clarity.
